newsitem.title: USA: NGPL plans to expand Iowa natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: NGPL plans to expand Iowa natgas pipeline.

text.p: Natural Gas Pipeline Co of America (NGPL) said Tuesday it will file a formal certificate application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to expand its Amarillo gas pipeline system between Harper, Iowa, and Chicago.
The expansion would be sufficient to transport all Canadian gas east of Harper, the company said in a statement.
A competing plan by Northern Border Pipeline Co, 70 percent owned by Enron Corp, proposed to build a new pipeline within a few miles of an existing line.

"The expansion of Natural's existing pipeline is a simple, cost-effective, environmentally sensitive solution. Northern Borders' proposal to build a new pipeline within a few miles of an existing line is undesirable for both environmental and economic reasons," NGPL vice president Dan Dodge said in prepared comments.
Both Natural's expansion and Northern Border's new pipeline to Chicago would be designed to handle new natural gas deliveries from Canada on an expanded Northern Border system.

Late last year, a draft environmental impact statement issued by FERC, which evaluated the proposed expansion of Natural's system and the proposed extension of the Northern Border system, concluded that having a single system alternative was preferable to both companies building new facilities east of Harper, the NGPL statement said.
In February, NGPL said Northern Border rejected its proposal that Northern should not build a new extension and instead contract for long-term transportation service on Natural's expanded line.
NGPL recommends that FERC establish a settlement conference at which interested parties can meet to address the matter, the statement added.
NGPL is a subsidiary of Midcon Corp, which is a unit of Occidental Petroleum Corp.
